SAR study · session logs only · generated

Two tiers, two scenarios

How operators used the Strategic and Tactical Assistants across the Strategic Heavy and Tactical Heavy scenarios, analysed as the 2×2 crossover the study actually ran. Surveys and recordings are left out on purpose; everything here comes from the event logs.

Build window
Outliers
1 · Design

Four games, not two

Everyone played seed 42, and until study-v1.13 the mission stream was seeded by seed ^ sessionNumber. So each scenario × run cell is one fixed game, played by only one of the two order groups. Run, order group and game are the same thing: "learning" and "the second game happened to be easier or richer" cannot be told apart from the logs alone. The imbalance is large: the Tactical Heavy game in run 2 asks for about 1.9× the work of the one in run 1, and the strategic-first group got the heavier game in both scenarios.

What survives. The scenario comparison averages two games per scenario, balanced across the order groups, so it's a fair comparison of these Tactical Heavy games against these Strategic Heavy games. The defining difference between scenarios (many small missions vs few large ones) holds in all four games. What doesn't. The run (learning) effect is confounded with the run-2 games carrying about 28% more work. Any order-group difference is confounded with game volume. Raw score isn't comparable across cells, so every performance figure uses score as a share of the points on offer. Reliance rates per decision are less exposed, and the decision-level models can be read alongside the logged momentary load.

2 · Performance

Score, not just completion

Score is what participants were chasing: points for completed tasks minus a penalty that grows while missions wait. Completion only counts whether tasks finished. The two agree only loosely (), so they can tell different stories.

Score per point on offer, by game

Each dot is one session; the bar is the cell mean. Lines connect the same scenario across runs, which means different people and a different game.

Raw score, by game

Grey ticks mark the points each game offered. The run-2 jump in raw score tracks them, not skill.

Crossover estimates

Scenario effect = Tactical Heavy minus Strategic Heavy; run effect = run 2 minus run 1, each with the other removed using the two order groups (Welch t). A significant interaction means the scenario gap depends on which came first. With four fixed games, that is also where a game-difficulty difference would show up. Run 2 only treats run 1 as a warm-up and compares the scenarios between people.

4 · Mission size

The bigger the mission, the more it gets handed to the Tactical Assistant

Mission categories run from A (small) to E (large). Scenario and size overlap heavily: Strategic Heavy is mostly A–B, Tactical Heavy is only C–E (). So each model below includes scenario and run alongside size.

Logistic GEE: use ~ category step + scenario + run, clustered by participant

Bottom: each participant's own slope (change in the chance of using the assistant per category step, from a straight-line fit). Right of zero means that person automated bigger missions more.

5 · Drone failures

Who abandons a mission that could have been saved?

Every drone failure opens a recovery. The log records whether the mission's own remaining drones could re-staff the broken task (feasibleWithOnMissionDrones, a per-task check), so an abandonment can be sorted into had to and chose to. Each recovery episode is classified by what the operator did before it closed.

7 · Outliers

Who, if anyone, to set aside

Robust z-scores (median / MAD) are computed within each of the four games, so a hard game doesn't make its players look like outliers. A participant is flagged only if they sit far below everyone else averaged over both runs (mean z < −2 on score per point on offer, or on number of decisions). One bad run isn't enough: a poor first run followed by a normal second one is learning, not noise. Completion isn't used to flag because it bunches at 80–90% and ordinary sessions reach |z| > 3. Flagged participants stay in the default view; the toggle at the top reruns every figure without them.

Method

How this page is made

Regenerate with python scripts/study_analysis.py (add --print for a text summary). Reads only Results/Participants/; participant ids are file names. Crossover tests follow the standard 2×2 analysis (Jones & Kenward) with Welch variance. Decision-level models are logistic GEEs with an exchangeable working correlation within participant, so a few hundred decisions from under twenty people aren't treated as independent. Rates are participant-averaged unless labelled "pooled". Numbers are in docs/reports/study_analysis.json. p-values are uncorrected and there are many of them: read the pattern, not any single star.
